Cyber Attack Disrupts Key Uzbek Infrastructure, Impacting Economy

TASHKENT, June 14 — A large-scale cyber attack targeting Uzbekistan’s national infrastructure has disrupted telecommunications, online payments, and key logistics networks, government officials said on Friday, raising concerns about the resilience of the country’s digital backbone.

Uzbektelecom JSC, the state-owned telecommunications provider, confirmed its networks had been compromised. “Our technical teams are working around the clock to restore services. Core communications and some internet connectivity remain unstable in several regions,” the company said in a statement.

Government ministries reported that the attack, which began late Thursday, has affected power grid monitoring systems and digital payment platforms, leading to delays at businesses and transport hubs nationwide. Access to mobile networks and broadband internet has been sporadic in Tashkent, Samarkand, and other major cities, residents said.

“We are confronting a coordinated cyber assault on critical infrastructure. Ensuring continued operation of essential services is our top priority,” Deputy Prime Minister Davron Tashkulov told reporters, without attributing blame or providing details about the perpetrators.

The Uzbekistan Association of Retailers said that electronic payment terminals were down at thousands of outlets, pushing many shops and cafes to accept cash only. “Small businesses are feeling the pressure, as customers are unable to use cards or mobile payments. This comes at a time when cashless transactions make up the majority of retail activity in urban centers,” said the group’s chairwoman Dilfuza Karimova.

Port operations at the key Navoi logistics hub have slowed as customs and cargo management systems experienced outages, according to a spokesperson for TransAsia Forwarding, a major transport company.

Cybersecurity analysts warned that the incident could have a lasting impact. “This attack exposes vulnerabilities in the interdependence of Uzbekistan’s digital infrastructure. Recovery will take time and may require international assistance,” said Timur Mukhamedov, a Tashkent-based information security consultant.

Authorities have not specified when full services will be restored. The Central Bank urged citizens to be patient, assuring that financial data remains secure. “We are working closely with telecom and payment providers to minimize disruption,” the bank said in a statement.
